newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods rise with NYMEX, refinery snag.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods rise with NYMEX, refinery snag.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast products edged higher Wednesday, on support from stronger New York futures markets and ongoing shutdowns at regional refineries, traders said.
A leak forced Arco on Monday to shut a 4,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker at its refinery in Carson, Calif.
The unit makes diesel and the problem resulted in a batch of off-spec fuel.
The company said it bought 60,000 barrels of diesel to cover the unit's lost output, sending
Meanwhile, prices for NYMEX heating oil rose just over two cents a gallon to 68.84 cents, with gasoline up 1.19 cents to 68.23 cents. Short covering of heating oil spurred the rally, traders said.
Offers for California CARB diesel rose one cent from Tuesday to 85 cents a gallon, while sellers of low sulphur grade asked for 74 cents a gallon, or 0.50 cents more than yesterday, traders said.

In gasoline markets, San Francisco conventional gasoline was sold at 76 Wednesday, even with Tuesday prices, traders said. Los Angeles conventional was the same price as the Bay grade, while CARB in L.A. rose a penny to 81/82 cents.
